Attach Cell Segmentation Polygons to a NICHESObject

Source: R/add_segmentation.R
add_segmentation.Rd

Stores a pre-built sf object of cell segmentation polygons in the $segmentation slot of a NICHESObject.

NICHESv2 does not extract segmentation data from Seurat objects – that step is platform-specific and belongs in the user's own preprocessing script. Once you have built an sf object (using sf), call this function to attach it so that downstream plotting utilities can overlay cell boundaries.

The sf object must have a cell column whose values are cell barcodes, and every cell in niches.obj$cell.list must have a corresponding polygon – since both the count matrix and the segmentation are extracted from the same source object, missing polygons indicate a barcode mismatch that must be resolved upstream. An error is raised if any cell is absent. Extra polygons for barcodes not in the object are permitted with a warning.

Usage

add_segmentation(niches.obj, seg.sf)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject.

seg.sf

An sf object with at least a cell column containing cell barcodes and an sf geometry column of cell polygons. Barcodes must match those in niches.obj$cell.list.

Value

The input NICHESObject with $segmentation populated.

See also

NICHESv2_example for an example object whose $segmentation slot is NULL and ready to receive an attached sf object; merge_NICHESObjects which uses sf::rbind() to combine $segmentation slots across merged objects.

Examples

# NICHESv2 expects 'seg.sf' to be an sf data.frame with:
#   * a 'cell' column matching niches.obj$cell.list
#   * an sf geometry column of polygons (one per cell)
# The exact construction is platform-specific (Visium HD, Xenium, MERFISH,
# CosMx, etc.). The skeleton below shows the required shape, using a unit
# square for every cell:
if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(NICHESv2_example)

  # Replace 'polygon.list' with polygons from your segmentation pipeline:
  polygon.list <- lapply(NICHESv2_example$cell.list, function(cell) {
    sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0),
                               ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)))
  })

  seg.sf <- sf::st_sf(
    cell     = NICHESv2_example$cell.list,
    geometry = sf::st_sfc(polygon.list)
  )

  niches.obj <- add_segmentation(NICHESv2_example, seg.sf)
}
#> [add_segmentation] Segmentation attached: 80 polygon(s) for 80 cell(s).
